flow.title: Solar Energy: From Sun to Storage
flow.summary: This 5-minute overview for teachers explains how solar energy is generated, stored, and its daily variation using a synthetic example dataset.

beats.title: How Solar Energy Works
beats.audienceText: Solar energy starts when sunlight passes through solar panels to generate electricity.
beats.speakerNotes: Explain that solar panels convert photons from the sun into electricity through the photovoltaic effect, which then charges batteries for later use.
beats.visualDirection: Show the diagram of Sun powering Panels which charge Battery

beats.title: Daily Energy Production
beats.audienceText: Solar production varies during the day, peaking at noon.
beats.speakerNotes: Highlight the synthetic example values showing energy generation is highest at noon when sunlight is strongest, and lowest in the morning/evening.
beats.visualDirection: Refer to the line chart showing Morning=10Wh, Noon=20Wh, Evening=5Wh

beats.title: Why Storage Matters
beats.audienceText: Storage makes solar energy available when sunlight is unavailable.
beats.speakerNotes: Conclude that energy storage enables solar power to be used even when the sun isn't shining, making renewable energy viable for daily use.
beats.visualDirection: Reiterate the diagram flow with emphasis on Battery as the final step
